newsitem.title: USA: Brazil tax reform urged by international banker.
newsitem.headline: Brazil tax reform urged by international banker.

text.p: Brazil is set to join the ranks of global economic powers but must sort out its taxation problems before growth can really take off, a top international banker said on Thursday.
Ronald Scheman, executive director of the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) for the United States, said he was optimistic and bullish about Brazil's prospects.
"The future has arrived. There is tremendous movement in the economy," he told Miami's Brazilian-American Chamber of Commerce.
But fiscal adjustment was needed to attract more foreign investment, and labour policies and high interest rates were also holding back a boom, Scheman said.

"It is working into the perception of the G-7 countries that Brazil is poised to enter the major economies," he said, referring to the Group of Seven (G-7) leading industrial nations. "It is clear that there is wise and intelligent management of the economy, which makes us hopeful for soft-landings in problem areas."
At present the tax burden was borne by a small base, he said. More efficient collection was needed as was a clarification of the powers of federal and state governments.
"You won't see private capital flowing in the way it could and should until you resolve fiscal adjustment," he said.

The lack of reforms meant the economy was relying on the exchange rate. That has forced high interest rates and restricted consumer spending. Banks and many small businesses had problems, Scheman said.
"What we hope to see in the coming year is the tax issue and the federal-state relationship are resolved, and at that time the economy will really take off," he said.
In Brasilia on Thursdsay, President Fernando Henrique Cardoso urged Congress to push ahead with approving fiscal reforms that have been bogged down for months.
In the two years since Cardoso came to power, businessmen say Brazil has begun to transform from a closed, uncompetitive and inflation-ridden economy into a global player.
